about: Enter the enchanting atmosphere of Café Nucleus Chatham, a captivating oasis nestled in the heart of Chatham's vibrant High Street. about: Set in the heart of 312 lush acres, Buxted Park is a glorious country hotel providing the perfect setting for the ultimate Afternoon Tea indulgence.  Built in 1722 by Sir Thomas Medley, Buxted Park Hotel's history is as colourful as it is long. The Grade II listed Palladian mansion, set in the finest parkland and the award-winning 2 AA Rosette dining, makes Buxted Park Hotel the ideal location to relax or celebrate.  The surroundings may be grand but that doesn’t mean a hushed reverence is encouraged. This great country house was built for pleasure, The Crystal Bar and Coat of Arms Lounge are special features of any visit to Buxted Park. Featuring decorative high ceilings, ornate chandeliers, full height windows with far reaching views of the estate and comfortable leather furniture, all serve to create a sense of grandeur, but one which will not stifle your occasion.  One of the most memorable experiences of Afternoon Tea East Sussex has to offer; you’ll be invited to sit down to a selection of delicious sweet and savoury treats served in one of the stunning lounges or on the terrace overlooking 300 acres of finest Ashdown Forest parkland.  Buxted Park Hotel is located in between Buxted and Uckfield, just a short distance from Buxted Station.

about: Enjoy Afternoon Tea in the epicentre of one of Britain's most historically exciting locations - Bletchley Park. Afternoon Tea price includes admission to park. Previously shrouded in secrecy to protect the nation's secrets, code breaking and developing technology defines Bletchley Park as it is the home of British intelligence. It is now open to visitors seven days a week, and enjoyed over 286,000 last year alone. It marries together the dramatic history of the twentieth century, with the challenges we face today. Visitors can explore experience and enjoy the top-secret world of iconic World War 2 Codebreaking Huts and Blocks set within its atmospheric Victorian estate. Reinvigorate yourself with Afternoon Tea, which is served in the dining room in the newly launched Mansion House. All food is created on site, with local ingredients. All the pastries and cakes are made daily by the passionate team of chefs. Located in Milton Keynes, Bletchley Park is opposite Bletchley railway station.

about: Please note Betsy's Tea Room is closed throughout December.  Alfonso La Cava opened St James Restaurant in Bushey Village in 1997. about: Indulge in an Afternoon Tea with a twist at Great Scotland Yard, a 5-star hotel where tradition and history meets modern luxury. The former home of the Metropolitan Police, this historical institution now fuses classic glamour with bold art. Every thoughtful detail of its interior design tells the story of its prominent past.  In collaboration with Floris London, The Parlour at Great Scotland Yard Hotel will launch its new summer Afternoon Tea bringing the Amalfi Coast to London this summer.  The Afternoon Tea is inspired by Floris London's “Bergamotto di Positano” fragrance, a refreshing blend of bergamot entwined with mandarin and balmy marine notes, orange blossom, vanilla and amber which encapsulates the signature aromas of the Amalfi Coast.  This Afternoon Tea collaboration promises to give guests ‘The faint sensation of forgotten summer hideaways that enflame hazy memories.’ The top notes of the fragrance have been skilfully interpreted into the menu with the introduction of typical ingredients of the coast and a re-interpretation of signature popular dishes of the Amalfitan culinary tradition, adapted to the setting of an afternoon tea. From Frittata di zucchine, particularly popular along the Amalfi Coast during summer, to Stracciatella, smoked salmon and caviar bruschetta which bring to the table the marine essence, the menu architecture has been carefully designed ensuring each dish has a story about Positano and the Amalfi Coast.  Warm scones are also served with Cornish Clotted Cream and Orange Jam, with a selection of sweet treats also available. These include the Almond & Cocoa Torta Caprese, Capri’s iconic cake, and Amalfi Lemon Delight “Delizia al Limone”, a priceless heritage that contains all the perfume and aroma of the “yellow gold” for excellence, the Limone Costa d’Amalfi I.G.P. (Protected Geographical Indication). In addition, the traditional babà with orange blossom, a traditional essence that pervades the houses of nonna along the coast during Spring will give guests a real taste of the coast.  The Afternoon Tea offers three irresistible options: For £59, savour the Standard Afternoon Tea, a delightful selection of savoury bites and sweet treats crafted to perfection. Alternatively, upgrade to the Pomello Spritz Afternoon Tea for £69 and enjoy the drink of the season – a refreshing Pomello Spritz cocktail, a grapefruit and elderflower aperitif, alongside your savoury and sweet treats.  Choose between Traditional Afternoon Tea, Champagne Afternoon Tea, or Bottomless Champagne Afternoon Tea with free-flowing Veuve Clicquot for 1.5 hours.  The hotel also welcomes furry friends for their Dog Afternoon Tea, which is available every Sunday. Further information about their Dog Afternoon Tea can be found here .  This iconic venue is steeped in history and would make the perfect pit stop from a day of sightseeing whilst continuing to absorb London's rich past. Located a stone's throw away from Covent Garden and one minute from Trafalgar Square, Great Scotland Yard Hotel connects Whitehall and Northumberland Avenue.  Please note that Great Scotland Yard require a card authentication in order to secure your booking. No shows or cancellations less than 24 hours in advance will be subject to a charge of £20 per person.
name: The Parlour at Great Scotland Yard Hotel

about: The five-star St James’s Hotel & Club is celebrating their rich history with a new Afternoon Tea menu. The Afternoon Tea showcases a selection of executive chef William Drabble’s expert creations, all based on authentic recipes and Queen Victoria’s favourites. about: Revery’s "Tea, Cakes & Cocktails" pays homage to the timeless tradition of Afternoon Tea while infusing it with contemporary flair. Crafted with love and care by Revery's award-winning pastry chefs, the menu features a delightful array of savoury and sweet treats.  In addition to the traditional tea offering, guests can also enjoy a mixology experience that includes one cocktail and one mocktail, prepared tableside for an interactive and personalised touch. The "Tea, Cakes & Cocktails" menu offers a unique selection of canapés, finger sandwiches, freshly baked scones, patisserie items, and the exclusive Revery pic ’n’ mix.  The tea begins with an array of canapés such as Beetroot Cheesecake and Mushroom Pate Tartlet, followed by the "Finger Feast" course featuring delicacies like Mini Poached Lobster Roll with Marie Rose Sauce and Devon Handpicked Crab on Sourdough Toast with Citrus Bisque Jelly. The sweet course includes Carrot Cheesecake, a Triple Chocolate Sandwich, and both Plain and Raisin Scones with Strawberry Jam and Clotted Cream. To cap off the experience, guests can enjoy the selection of Revery’s pic ’n’ mix, including Apple Jelly, Vanilla Fudge, and Dark Chocolate Truffle.  To complement the tasty treats, Revery is delighted to partner with London Tea Exchange, providing a selection of over 300 premium and rare teas sourced from twenty different countries. These teas, some of the rarest and most sought-after by connoisseurs globally, ensure an unparalleled tea-tasting experience.  Revery takes the experience a step further, setting itself apart from the traditional British Afternoon Tea with a selection of perfectly paired and meticulously crafted cocktails, ranging from an Earl Grey Sour to the Pistachio Bliss – a blend of pistachio liqueur, amaretto, and cream. Non-alcoholic options include the Blooming Blossom, featuring elderflower syrup and fresh strawberries, and the Moroccan Souk – an exotic blend of orange juice, ginger, cinnamon, and mint.

about: The Petersham, in the heart of Covent Garden is serving La Merenda, an Afternoon Tea inspired by the café culture of Turin. Drawing on the Boglione family’s Piedmontese heritage, the menu combines the quintessential British afternoon tea with the vibrant flavours and delicious produce of Italy.  The Boglione family have created a business that inspires, celebrates and shares exceptional knowledge, passion and creativity. This has naturally evolved from their personal passion into a thriving business. In turn they have established a culture and raised a ‘Petersham’ family of likeminded individuals who share their lifelong passion for organic gardening, culinary excellence, ethical and sustainable sourcing, as well as drawing out beauty in the simplest of things.  Guests can settle into the grandeur of The Petersham’s high-ceilinged dining room, filled with Murano glassware and contemporary art, with a glass of Champagne as they read through the menu.  La Merenda begins with tramezzini, small sandwiches prepared with soft white milk bread, invented in Turin in the 1920s as an alternative to English tea sandwiches.  Lorenzo Gagliradi, the executive chef at Petersham Nurseries, will be serving puff pastry pizzette, which are meticulously garnished with fresh seasonal ingredients from the like tomato, anchovies, capers, and briny olives; or asparagus, smoky scamorza cheese, and lemon.  Lastly for the dolci, a variety of sweet delights that draw inspiration from Turin's standing as one of Italy's capitals of chocolate and traditional desserts. In addition to tea, guests at The Petersham can choose from an assortment of hot beverages that are inspired by the coffee shops of Turin.

about: Blenheim Palace invites guests to join them for Afternoon Tea in the newly refurbished Orangery Restaurant reopening in October 2023.    In January 2023, the team at Blenheim Palace embarked on an innovative conservation project to reinstate the roof of The Orangery to its original slate composition. It is the first Grade 1 listed building to carry out a project of this kind. This process involved the removal of the existing glass ceiling, replacing it with a hand-crafted timber and slate structure. Over the course of the last three centuries, The Orangery has fulfilled a range of roles, from a greenhouse and conservatory to a theatre, an art gallery, office spaces, and most recently a restaurant.    Experience elegant dining with their Afternoon Tea menu, featuring authentically British, house-made scones, delightful, sweet treats, and an array of dainty sandwiches.  Blenheim Palace sits at the edge of the idyllic town of Woodstock, just 20 minutes from Oxford. It is also within easy reach of Birmingham and Central London. about: Afternoon Tea Awards 2024 - 'Award of Excellence'  Dust off your Regency best, as The Lanesborough presents a new Afternoon Tea experience inspired by Bridgerton. The latest in their innovative series of seasonal Afternoon Teas, the limited-edition menu pays homage to the Regency era; a time of great revelling and high style, of elegant parties, balls, and grand dinners, with a contemporary twist.  Setting the scene, the Bridgerton Afternoon Tea takes place in The Lanesborough’s richly decorated Regency dining room, naturally illuminated during the day by a domed glass roof.  Carefully crafted by our Head Pastry Chef, Pierre Morvan-Benezet, the menu pays tribute to the key families in Bridgerton Season 3 and is comprised of a selection of finger sandwiches and pastry tartlets, delectable scones, cream and jam, and four signature sweet treats.  The menu features four signature sweet treats inspired by the show’s main characters, as well as the ‘Friends to Lovers’ cocktail inspired by Lady Whistledown which makes for a wonderful alternative to Champagne (a non-alcoholic cocktail is also available).  Situated moments from Hyde Park in Knightsbridge, this landmark building of 1828 has been restored to its original splendour and is one of London's finest 5 star premier hotels. about: Afternoon Tea Awards 2024 - Award of Excellence  L’oscar London, a luxurious boutique hotel, have launched their new Afternoon Tea, inspired by the historical grade II* listed building that was once the headquarters of the Baptist Church.  L’oscar London is located in the heart of London’s Southampton Row, close to Covent Garden, Theatreland, Soho, and the West End. Built between 1901 and 1903, in a style coined “Edwardian Free Baroque”, it was the London headquarters of the Baptist Church, and has since been restored by world renowned French decorator, Jacques Garcia.  Afternoon Tea at L’oscar is served in L’oscar Restaurant which features an illuminated Onyx bar with ceilings lined with mirrors, gilded panels and stunning original art. The restaurant offers all the charm and sophistication of a Parisian café. In true tradition, guests can expect delicious savoury and dainty sandwiches including roast heritage beef, caramelised onions, gherkins and watercress on tomato bread, and smoked Scottish salmon roulade with keda caviar and chervil on rye bread. Sweet treats on offer include delicately crafted cakes such as a chocolate & pistachio praline tart and a Choux Bun with white wine rhubarb & strawberry compote.  To cleanse the palate, guests can choose from flutes of Champagne or a selection of loose tea leaves from Newby.  Afternoon Tea is served Friday – 2:30pm – 5:00pm and Saturday & Sunday – 12:00pm – 5:00pm and costs £59 per person, or £69 with a glass of Champagne.

about: Afternoon Tea Awards 2019 - Highly Commended  Secret Garden Afternoon Tea  The Secret Garden Afternoon Tea which will transport diners to a stunning Yorkshire Garden with every bite. The beautifully designed pastries and delectable savoury treats have been inspired by the timeless children’s classic tale of The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett.  The menu includes fresh, seasonal sandwiches including Garden herb roast chicken and Cucumber, beetroot and basil butter. Delight in a range of sumptuous sweet treats, from Fair Fresh Leaves – a mandarin citrus cream cheese tart baked with basil almond cream, to Leaves and Trees Flowers and Birds – a moist olive oil and lime cake with a mango ganache.  The Secret Garden Afternoon Tea is complemented with a selection of teas from Bird & Blend Tea Co. From leaf to cup, each tea has been carefully selected to pair beautifully with the sweet and savoury offering. For those looking to upgrade their experience, the magic is in the gin. The Secret Garden Gin Distillery has partnered with Kona to deliver the wonder of nature and unique flavours with three different Gins.  When guests are ready to begin, they will be able to communicate this by opening a bespoke box on the table that once opened will release a flutter of nature to signify it is time for tea. All guests will receive a complementary keepsake of wildflower seeds so they can plant their very own secret garden at home.  The Secret Garden Afternoon Tea is available from £75 per person.  Indian Jasmine Afternoon Tea  Jasmine Indian Afternoon Tea is also available, which evokes the rich traditions of the Indian dining culture with a bold and innovative twist on the traditional Afternoon Tea.  Enjoy a variety of sandwiches such as Minced mutton pinwheel in white bread and savoury Eastern dishes such as Aloo Bonda Mango Chutney Bun. Follow with the traditional Indian dessert Gulab Jamun and a selection of delicious cakes, scones and pastries, including Cheesecake Raspberry Sonpapri Floss and Saffron & Elaichi scones.  Wash it down with a selection of eastern and western teas and coffees or a delicious Masala Chai.  The Jasmine Afternoon Tea is available from £75 per person.  Just a stone's throw from Buckingham Palace, Kona is nestled in the 5-star Taj 51 Buckingham Gate Suites and Residences, a prestigious and luxury hotel.

about: Afternoon tea at Jean-Georges puts a playful, contemporary twist on this time-honoured British tradition. Allow them to whisk you away on a sensational journey through taste and texture in the heart of London – with a few unexpected surprises along the way.  Jean-Georges at The Connaught sets a bright and lively scene for an afternoon tea with a twist. The experience begins the moment you step into this stylish neighbourhood restaurant in Mayfair. Curated art from Louise Bourgeois adorns the walls and floor to ceiling windows, with their stained-glass accents by Jean-Michel Othoniel, give you the perfect vantage point to watch the world of Mayfair go by. Then, it’s time to open the menu – its playful illustrations by Jean Jullien hinting at the bold flavours and witty surprises soon to unfold.  Begin your taste adventure as you discover a selection of exotic teas – or, a glass of champagne, if you want to add some sparkle to the afternoon. Then it’s on to the finger sandwiches, where classic British combinations meet Jean-Georges’ passion for bold South East-Asian flavours. Think cucumber with a hint of mint, oak smoked salmon, and turkey and tandoori yoghurt in Mediterranean bread, all home-made daily.  For a touch of tradition, their cakes are accompanied by English scones prepared to a time-honoured recipe. These are served warm from the oven, ready for spreading with Cornish clotted cream and homemade strawberry jam.

about: Centuries may separate Elizabeth I and Elizabeth II’s reigns, yet here, their tales intertwine. Together, their shared love for decadent teas and confections shaped the sophisticated tradition of Afternoon Tea as we know it.  InterContinental London Park Lane Invite you to sample the tastes of the two distinguished queens with a delectable array of finely crafted sweet delicacies and savoury delights hailing from noble menus of past and present.Each morsel is served on the finest Renaissance Gold teaware set by Wedgwood, a Royal Warrant holder, for an authentic regal experience. Dine like a true monarch with desserts such as our rhubarb and champagne syllabub with sablé biscuit, a favourite of the 16th-century Elizabeth, before relishing a rich chocolate biscuit cake inspired by our late queen’s affinity for the treat. No afternoon tea is complete without an assortment of savoury sandwiches to balance the sweet pastries, especially our coronation chicken sandwich. This flavour sensation is our modern interpretation of the 1953 invention served at Elizabeth II’s coronation luncheon. about: Afternoon Tea Awards 2024 - Award of Excellence  Avaliable 6th May - 31st August 2024  In homage to Queen Elizabeth’s majestic flair and with Royal Ascot just around the corner, Brown’s has pulled it out of the hat and created an Afternoon Tea extravaganza bursting with hat-themed delights that we have no doubt her late Majesty herself would have enjoyed.  Inspired by royal tea parties and elegant gatherings where ladies donned their finest attire, each of the Couture hats are a work of art in themselves and have been meticulously designed by Awon Golding, Head Millinery Designer, on the top floor of the St James’s Street shop. In turn, guests are invited to dress for the occasion and savour sweet and savoury treats in Brown’s oak-panelled Drawing Room, which will be filled to the brim with the pastel and floral hat  pieces, such as the Rose Bud Leather Percher Hat and the Lady Grey Black Wide Brim Hat. The limited-edition Afternoon Tea menu will feature tea-infused and delicate hat-shaped cakes, chouxbuns, and scones served, silver service style, from one of Lock & Co’s iconic hat boxes. With all of the hats named after different types of tea, guests are sure to delight in choosing from the 26 varieties of tea on the menu.  Brown's Hotel has a fascinating history and has hosted many distinguished guests since it opened as London's first ever hotel in 1832. It is from here that Rudyard Kipling penned many of his novels and it is believed that this elegant setting was the inspiration for Agatha Christie's 'At Bertram's Hotel'. To this day this glamorous, five-star establishment welcomes guests 'in-the-know'.  The Drawing Room serves one of the most famous Afternoon Teas in London and was awarded a Commended certificate at the Afternoon Tea Awards 2019 in recognition of their quality. The sophisticated and stylish interior is a clever mix of both tradition - thanks to the original wood paneling, fire places and Jacobean detailed plaster ceiling and contemporary style, with Paul Smith lighting, fashionable fabrics and original artworks.  Relax to the sounds from the Baby Grand Piano and indulge in a choice of 17 teas, including Brown's own blend, along with a selection of succulent finger sandwiches, an assortment of delicate pastries, fruit and plain scones with clotted cream and strawberry preserve, as well as a choice of freshly baked cakes from the trolley. Guests of The Drawing Room never leave hungry, as the finger sandwiches are continuously replenished at no additional charge.  No matter what a guest's dietary requirements may be, from gluten free to nut allergies, the team of chefs at Brown's Hotel will ensure that everyone has the chance to enjoy their award-winning Afternoon Tea. 48 hours advanced notice is required to prepare these special teas.  Your table will be available for 1 hour 45 minutes. A cancellation made with less than 48 hours notice, incurs a cancellation fee of £30 per guest.

about: Dalchini, the UK’s first authentic Indo-Chinese restaurant, has launched its very own one of a kind afternoon tea in Wimbledon. Balancing  British tradition with the rich tapestry of Indo-Chinese flavours, it includes finger sandwiches, Indian and Chinese savouries, freshly baked scones, muffins and cakes, alongside a large tea selection and Prosecco.  Finger sandwiches come filled with Grilled Mediterranean Vegetables and Garlic Mayo, and Shredded Chicken infused with Black Pepper, followed by a selection of Indian and Chinese snacks – think Aloo Mutter Samosa, Sesame Prawn Toast, and Crisply Chilli Garlic Paneer.  Sweet treats nod to the quintessential British offering with Freshly Baked Raisins & Cheddar Scones served with Cornish Clotted Cream and Strawberry Jam alongside in-house baked Chocolate & Vanilla Muffins, Brownies and a Fruit Tea Cake.  All served either inside the restaurant, or on their intimate seating outside. Guests can pick from an extensive selection of world teas – Flavoured Black Tea from Sri Lanka, Oolong from Taiwan and Camomile tea from Egypt to name a few – or opt for a glass of Prosecco.  Indo-Chinese cuisine traces back to the late 19th century when Hakka Chinese migrants settled in Kolkata, India, and you can get a taste of it at 25 year old Dalchini, the first to bring these flavours to the UK, and now in an Afternoon Tea. about: Celebrate the Coronation with an Afternoon Tea that’s fit for a king.  The new Crown Afternoon Tea at Vintry and Mercer is a truly majestic gastronomic experience, and a new twist on what has long been considered a great British institution. Join them to raise a glass to the Royals and mark a historic event in the British calendar!  Each beautifully presented serving comes bedecked with the finest sweet and savory treats. To start, enjoy delicious smoked salmon and cream cheese sandwiches, coronation chicken vol-au-vons with mango chutney, roast beef, horseradish and gravy ‘Yorkshire pudding’ and truffled egg mayonnaise brioche buns, each named after one of the famous Royal Palaces. Enjoy with a glass of Charles Heidsieck Brut NV or Rose Champagne, or Wild Idol alcohol free sparkling rose, and a selection of teas. At Vintry and Mercer, dining is as much a part of the experience as the overnight stay. Whether at our rooftop restaurant, cocktail bar or all-day eatery, guests will find bold, flavourful cuisine matched with original cocktails and world-class wine.  In one sweep, the view from Mercer Roof Terrace takes in London’s skyline, from the dome of St Paul’s Cathedral to the glass tip of The Shard. Inside, the atmosphere is warm and convivial, with floor-to-ceiling glass doors opening wide to bring the outdoors in.  Crown Afternoon Tea is available on Saturdays and Sundays.

about: Cliveden House is the ultimate location to partake in a quaint Afternoon Tea - this grand five-star hotel boasts an aristocratic heritage, lavish décor and immaculate gardens. A Grade I listed stately home, Cliveden House has been the luxury destination for Britain's elite since it was built in 1666.  To honour the estate’s legacy, Executive Head Chef, Christopher Hannon and his team curated a comprehensive Cliveden history inspired Afternoon Tea.  This culinary homage honours key features, such as the French Chocolate Cake symbolizing the elegant French Dining Room, originally from Château d'Asnières near Paris, the 24-carat Gold Pickled Egg representing the Octagon Chapel where William Waldorf rests, and the artistic Cliveden Four Seasons Fruit Cake showcasing the ceiling mural portraying the Duchess of Sutherland's four children as the seasons of the year.  This culinary celebration beautifully encapsulates the essence of Cliveden House, where social aspirations were realised, and political history unfolded.  If you visit during the week, expect to be seated in the beautiful The Cliveden Dining Room where Afternoon Tea is served amongst ornate period features. On Sundays, you can enjoy this traditional dining experience in the distinguished surroundings of The Great Hall.  Complete your visit by enjoying a stroll around the beautiful 376 estate. An additional charge of £10 is levied by the National Trust for all guests visiting Cliveden House although if you are already a National Trust member there is no extra charge.

about: Cally Palace, on the outskirts of the pretty village of Gatehouse of Fleet on the Solway coast, is set in over 150 acres of grounds. about: Hidden away for 900 years near the picturesque village of Amberley in the chalk South Downs, Amberley Castle is a magnificent historical treasure that offers a truly unique experience.
